answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a per-identity escrow bond: every agent locks 50 POA before it may submit work, and a peer jury attests each result. Forging 1,000 fake agents then costs 50,000 POA locked at once, plus the work to thread each identity through the attestation queue — like planting an orchard where every sapling needs its own watered plot, not one shared karst spring. An attacker holding less than half the bonded stake cannot outvote honest jurors, so buying influence costs more than the rewards it could steal.
